veranderings.rede: The compound verb 'gaarkook' (like 'gaarmaak') is written as one word, so it is joined in this subordinate clause.
Used as a noun, the compound verb 'saameet' (like 'saamwerk') is written as one word.

veranderings.voor: wat die land se wette en regering amptelik erken
veranderings.na: wat deur die land se wette en regering amptelik erken word
veranderings.rede: The active relative clause can be misread as the language recognising the laws; the passive makes clear the laws and government recognise the language (adds two words).

vlae.teks: Stampmielies en boontjies wat lank saam in een pot gaar kook.
vlae.rede: Same spelling fault as in the study block ('gaar kook' should be 'gaarkook'), but this wording also occurs almost verbatim in the study text, so no unique 'voor' can be given; the glossary entry should match whatever the study text ends up with.
